clue.text: Confident, like retiring American left-winger

parts.note: like means as, in the sense of similar to

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the short form for American is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a socialist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: A self-assured American socialist is stepping down from public life.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone sure of themselves is self-confident.

clue.text: Agree to clubs participating in expert training

indicators.note: participating in means the clubs letter goes inside the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Golf clubs agree to take part in a specialist's coaching course.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to consent to an offer is to agree to it.

clue.text: One's endeavouring to spot king and queen

definitions.note: one who is trying or searching, a noun phrase

parts.note: to spot is to see
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is trying hard to catch sight of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person who seeks is trying to find something, so is endeavouring.

clue.text: Revived a festival introduced by Magritte and Dali, originally

indicators.note: introduced by means the festival is brought inside the painters' letters

parts.note: René Magritte, the Belgian surrealist painter
a wake is a local festival or holiday, especially in northern England

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of Dali is used

explanation.surface: Two surrealist painters breathed new life into an arts festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A wake is a local annual holiday in northern England, not only a vigil for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: brought back to life or consciousness is revived.

clue.text: Press campaign

definitions.meaning: to press is to push or urge on
a campaign is an organised effort, such as a fundraising push

explanation.surface: A newspaper crusade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to push hard is to press, and an organised effort is a campaign.

clue.text: Perform check, covering county where Homer settled?

definitions.note: a homer is a homing pigeon, which roosts in a pigeon house

parts.note: to perform a task is to do it

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps round the other, so the word for check goes round the county

parts.note: to vet something is to check it over

explanation.surface: Someone carries out a check on the region where the Greek poet Homer made his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer is not the poet but a homing pigeon; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a homing pigeon settles in a pigeon house, the shelter where such birds live.

clue.text: Furore following elevated journalist's stay

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, which in a down clue reverses the journalist's letters

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist
a ferment is a state of agitation or uproar

explanation.surface: A furore over a promoted reporter's suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses the editor because this is a down entry, read upwards; 'following' puts the uproar after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a postponement, as in a stay of execution, is a putting-off.

clue.text: Worthless classical poet promoting his verse

indicators.note: promoting means moving a letter higher, here up one place in a down entry

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an ancient poet who keeps pushing his own poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' lifts V from third place to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense: a contract that is null and has no legal force is worthless.

clue.text: Processed grain etc, providing food

indicators.note: processed means the letters of grain etc are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Refined cereals and the like make up the food on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the business of supplying meals for events is the providing of food.

clue.text: See through end of telescope in port after it's set up

indicators.note: after means the port piece follows the reversed it
set up in a down clue means the word it is raised and so read upwards
in means the last letter of telescope goes inside the port

parts.note: Dover is the Channel port in Kent

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of telescope

explanation.surface: Someone peers through a telescope after setting it up in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IT to TI; 'in' puts E into DOVER. Dover is England's main ferry port to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to tide someone over is to help them through a hard spell, to see them through.

clue.text: Shell uncovered beside cape — a crab's disabled without it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of the word shell are stripped off, leaving its inside

explanation.surface: A crab caught without its shell near a headland is left helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' does double duty: it supplies the last letter and opens the definition, a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the pincer claw of a crab or lobster is what it grips and feeds with, so losing one disables it.

clue.text: Visited area excluded from redraft of final edict

indicators.note: excluded from means the letter for area is left out of the fodder before it is rearranged
a redraft rewrites a text, so the letters of final edict are rearranged

explanation.surface: A local district was left out when an official order was rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from FINAL EDICT and rearrange the remaining FINLEDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense: to visit a punishment on someone is the old phrasing for imposing or dealing it out.

clue.text: Girlfriend installed in Frenchman's love nest, maybe

indicators.note: installed in means one piece is placed inside the other, the girlfriend inside the Frenchman

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is someone you go out with romantically

explanation.surface: A Frenchman sets his girlfriend up in a secret flat.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE + DATE + RRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small second flat kept in town can serve as a discreet place for an affair, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Expressed regret for euro, say

definitions.note: a euro is a species of wallaroo, a kind of kangaroo

indicators.note: Expressed means spoken out, so the word for regret is heard rather than read

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone voiced regret about the single European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The euro is not money here but a large Australian marsupial, also called the common wallaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the euro is one kind of kangaroo, for which this is the short Australian name.

clue.text: Insular Spaniard working as cathedral junior

parts.note: a Minorcan is a native of the Spanish island Minorca
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A Spanish islander takes a lowly job at a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a clergyman attached to a cathedral but below the full canons ranks as a cathedral junior.

clue.text: Priest in country after a spell oddly lost independence

indicators.note: after means the country piece comes after the letters from a spell
oddly lost means the odd-numbered letters of a spell go, leaving the second, fourth and sixth
in means the priest is placed inside the country

parts.note: France is the country
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric abroad, after a stretch of time, lost his freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly lost' drops the first, third and fifth letters of 'a spell'; 'in' puts the priest inside the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relying on yourself rather than others is being independent.

clue.text: Preferred winding route via south of France

indicators.note: south of means in a down entry the shuffled letters go below the France letter

parts.note: F is the international code for France

indicators.note: winding means the letters of route via twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A favourite twisting road through southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the one most liked or chosen first is the preferred one.

clue.text: Remove clogs, seeing good time ahead

indicators.note: ahead means the good time piece comes before the clogs piece

parts.note: an up is a good time, as in ups and downs
clogs, as a verb, means jams or sticks

explanation.surface: Someone takes off their wooden shoes because they are early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' means move house: the phrase is British slang for packing up and leaving. Clogs looks like shoes but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: British informal phrase for packing up and moving to live elsewhere, so to remove or relocate.

clue.text: Put an end to trusted criminal carrying drug

indicators.note: carrying means the rearranged letters hold the drug letter inside them
criminal means the letters of trusted are bent out of shape

parts.note: C is short for cocaine

explanation.surface: A trusted crook smuggling narcotics is to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TRUSTED to DESTRUT, and 'carrying' takes C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something wipe itself out, as with a rocket, is to put an end to it.

clue.text: Keeping quiet, with some little doubt

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
a reservation is a mild doubt or qualm

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent while harbouring a small misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: keeping something safe and unchanged is protecting it from decay.

clue.text: Curmudgeon in receipt of Nutmeg's misdirected delivery?

indicators.note: in receipt of means the bear receives the setter inside

parts.note: a bear is a grumpy person, as in a bear with a sore head
Nutmeg is the setter of this puzzle, so Nutmeg's is me

explanation.surface: A grump receives a parcel from the setter that went to the wrong address.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery is the cricket sense: a beamer is a full toss aimed, usually by accident, at the batsman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in cricket a ball bowled straight at head height without bouncing is a wayward delivery.

clue.text: Where you'd expect a barrister from superior chambers?

definitions.text: Where you'd expect a barrister from superior chambers?

parts.words: Where you'd expect a barrister from superior chambers
parts.note: a barrister is expected in court while a case is heard; superior chambers read as the upper cavities of the heart

explanation.surface: A barrister from a top set of chambers would be expected in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly the word suggests 'at trial'; barristers work from chambers, but superior chambers are the upper cavities of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: the adjective describing the two upper cavities of the heart, which receive blood from the veins.

clue.text: Rubbish article in Times

indicators.note: in means the article is placed inside the letters for Times

parts.note: T stands for time, so two of them give times
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of junk writing appears in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Times is not the newspaper but T for time, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cheap tasteless junk is called rubbish or tat in British slang.

clue.text: Adequate turnover for Guardian, working well without capital

indicators.note: turnover for means the word standing for the newspaper is turned round

parts.note: this puzzle appears in the Guardian, which refers to itself as us

indicators.note: without capital means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: efficient means working well

explanation.surface: The Guardian's turnover is healthy apart from a lack of investment funds.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's newspaper is US, turned to SU; EFFICIENT loses its first letter to make FFICIENT. Capital and turnover are business words with letter jobs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: enough for the purpose is adequate.

clue.text: Upset roughly one litre of pharmaceutical acid

definitions.note: the answer names a vitamin acid, used in the phrase for the B vitamin; here it stands for the acid

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for roughly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over about a litre of medicinal acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses CILOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this B vitamin, sold as a supplement for pregnancy, is an acid made by drug companies.

clue.text: Damage statuette, knocking head off

indicators.note: knocking head off means the first letter of the word for statuette is removed

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award statuette

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a little statue by knocking its head off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mark or disfigure something is to damage it.

clue.text: Body of Christians threatening war leader

parts.note: a church is a body of Christian believers
ill can mean ominous, as in an ill omen

explanation.surface: A congregation of worshippers is menacing a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill was Britain's Prime Minister through most of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Britain's Prime Minister in the Second World War was its leader in wartime.

clue.text: Review of global IT firm in Sky features

indicators.note: review of is read as re-view, looking back, so the words are reversed

parts.note: IBM is the multinational computer company

explanation.surface: A critique of a computer giant appears in the Sky TV channel's programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review of' reverses IBM IN to give NIMBI. Sky is not the broadcaster but the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rain clouds and haloes are things seen in the heavens, and this is their plural.

clue.text: Release bargain offer for telly addicts?

definitions.meaning: to release a prisoner is to liberate them
read as a television that costs nothing, a giveaway for keen viewers

explanation.surface: A promotion that lets television fans go wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym and pun: liberate means release, and read another way it is a free TV.

clue.text: Hold back company books and most of inventory

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for inventory is dropped

parts.note: a roll is a list or register

explanation.surface: A firm withholds its accounts and much of its stock list.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to restrain something is to hold it back or keep it in check.
